name: Subscription waste
seoDesc: Subscription waste: work out total cost per month from the cost per month. A free finance calculator with the formula, units and a worked example.
summary: The Subscription waste calculator takes the numbers you enter and reports total cost per month immediately. It is free to use, needs no account, and shows the working rather than just the answer. It suits a budget, a loan conversation, a payslip check or a what-if before you talk to a lender. Every field is labelled the way you would say it out loud, so you can usually fill the form from memory and only look up the numbers you genuinely do not know.

sections.title: How does the Subscription waste calculator work?
sections.html:
The Subscription waste calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports total cost per month in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case (the service #1 (Streaming TV), the service #2 (Streaming TV) and the service #3 (Streaming TV)); then you type in the cost per month (Streaming TV), the cost per month (Streaming TV), the cost per month (Streaming TV) and the cost per month (E-Commerce & Delivery).

Press Calculate once and the page holds the relationship, tracking which boxes you filled and working out everything else; from that point on it follows every edit you make.

sections.title: The formula behind the Subscription waste calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Total cost per month=((cost per month + cost per month) + (cost per month + cost per month) + (cost per month + cost per month) + (cost per month + cost per month) + (cost per month + cost per month + cost per month) + (cost per month + cost per month + cost per month) + (cost per month + cost per month + cost per month) + (other service #1 + other service #2 + other service #3 + other service #4 + other service #5))
!!Total cost per month!!=(cost per month + cost per month + cost per month)
!!Total cost per month!!=(cost per month + cost per month)
!!Total cost per month!!=(other service #1 + other service #2 + other service #3 + other service #4 + other service #5)
Total cost per year=(12 × ((cost per month + cost per month) + (cost per month + cost per month) + (cost per month + cost per month) + (cost per month + cost per month) + (cost per month + cost per month + cost per month) + (cost per month + cost per month + cost per month) + (cost per month + cost per month + cost per month) + (other service #1 + other service #2 + other service #3 + other service #4 + other service #5)))

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: What is a worked example?
sections.html:
Take Service #1 set to Netflix, cost per month = 10, Service #2 set to Netflix and cost per month = 10. The calculator returns !!Total cost per month!! = 30, Total cost per month = 220 and Total cost per year = 2640.

Read it as a template. Every number above can be replaced with one of yours; only the relationship between them is fixed.

  1. Enter the values listed above, matching the units each box asks for.
  2. Read off the result. Any field you leave empty is the one the calculator solves for.
  3. Sanity-check the number against the relationship: !!Total cost per month!! = 30, Total cost per month = 220 and Total cost per year = 2640 should be roughly the size you expected from Service #1 set to Netflix and cost per month = 10.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Subscription waste calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Building a monthly budget and testing how one number shifts the rest
  • Preparing questions for a lender, an accountant or an adviser
  • Sizing up a purchase before you commit to it
  • Any time the same 1 figures keep coming back — the cost per month — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.
  • If a result surprises you, look at the order of magnitude before the digits: a plausible number in the wrong unit looks more convincing than an implausible one, and is easier to miss.
  • Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.
  • Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.

faq.q: What does the Subscription waste calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns total cost per month, derived from the cost per month. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Subscription waste calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the cost per month, which is 39 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There are several choices to make (17 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

With the values the page starts from, the calculator reports !!Total cost per month!! = 30. Treat that as a reference point rather than a recommendation: it exists so you can tell at a glance whether your own inputs are on the same scale.

faq.q: Is the Subscription waste calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — press Calculate and every result updates together.
